description_full: Equinox Gold Corp. engages in the acquisition, exploration, development, and operation of mineral properties in the Americas. It primarily explores gold and silver deposits. The company was formerly known as Trek Mining Inc. and changed its name to Equinox Gold Corp. in December 2017. Equinox Gold Corp. was incorporated in 2007 and is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada.

financial_summary: Equinox Gold Corp. is a large-cap basic materials business with a $12.3B market cap on $1.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +24% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 3% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 20% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $126M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.70× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.2× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 2.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.5%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 3.4% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

Trade policy and tariff whiplash — materials producers are first-order casualties of protectionist swings, and margin gets squeezed from both input and output pricing.
